The '''2011–12 Ligue 1 season''' was the 74th since its establishment.<ref>{{cite news|title=Palmarès: Les champions de France depuis 1932/1933 |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/palmares |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |access-date=23 April 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110419073300/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/palmares |archive-date=19 April 2011 }}</ref> [[Lille OSC|Lille]] were the [[2010–11 Ligue 1|defending champions]]. The league schedule was announced on 31 March 2011 and the fixtures were determined on 10 June.<ref>{{cite news|title=Le calendrier dévoilé le 10 juin |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/breves2011/20110530_140030_le-calendrier-devoile-le-10-juin.html |work=[[L'Equipe]] |date=30 May 2011 |access-date=30 May 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110602131338/http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/breves2011/20110530_140030_le-calendrier-devoile-le-10-juin.html |archive-date=2 June 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Les calendriers 2011/2012 |url=http://new.lfp.fr/corporate/article/les-calendriers-2011-2012.htm |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=10 June 2011 |access-date=21 June 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119111703/http://new.lfp.fr/corporate/article/les-calendriers-2011-2012.htm |archive-date=19 January 2012 }}</ref> The season began on 6 August 2011 and ended on 20 May 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=2011-2012 : Reprise le 6 août |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/breves2011/20110211_141128_2011-2012-reprise-le-6-aout.html |work=[[L'Equipe]] |date=31 March 2011 |access-date=22 April 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110515070006/http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/breves2011/20110211_141128_2011-2012-reprise-le-6-aout.html |archive-date=15 May 2011 }}</ref> The winter break was in effect from 22 December 2011 to 14 January 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=Le calendrier général 2011-2012 validé |url=http://new.lfp.fr/calendriers/2011_2012/calendrier_2011_2012.pdf |work=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=31 March 2011 |access-date=22 April 2011 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110823041848/http://new.lfp.fr/calendriers/2011_2012/calendrier_2011_2012.pdf |archive-date=2011-08-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 20 May 2012, the final day of the league season, [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] clinched its first-ever league title after defeating [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]] 2–1 at the [[Stade de l'Abbé-Deschamps]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Montpellier wins French title for first time |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/soccer/wires/05/20/2080.ap.soc.french.roundup.2nd.ld.writethru.0916/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313003755/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/soccer/wires/05/20/2080.ap.soc.french.roundup.2nd.ld.writethru.0916/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 13, 2014 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=20 May 2012 |access-date=20 May 2012 |language = fr}}</ref>  Montpellier was the fifth different club to win Ligue 1 since the [[2007–08 Ligue 1|2007–08 season]] and qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time in its history. [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] and [[Lille OSC|Lille]] were the country's other Champions League participants, while [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], and [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] represented France in the [[UEFA Europa League]]. Lyon did not participate in [[UEFA]]'s top football club competition for the first time in 12 years.

[[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]], [[Dijon FCO|Dijon]], and [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]] were relegated to [[2012–13 Ligue 2|Ligue 2]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dijon et Caen relégués en Ligue 2 |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-actu/2012/05/20/97001-20120520FILWWW00252-foot-dijon-et-caen-relegues-en-ligue-2.php |work=Le Figaro |date=20 May 2012|access-date=20 May 2012 |language = fr}}</ref> Auxerre returned to the second division after 32 consecutive years playing in Ligue 1.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ligue 1 : L'AJ Auxerre relégué 42 ans après! |url=http://journal.football.fr/post/2012/05/14/ligue-1-laj-auxerre-relegue-42-ans-apres |work=Football.fr |date=14 May 2012 |access-date=18 May 2012 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120517004425/http://journal.football.fr/post/2012/05/14/ligue-1-laj-auxerre-relegue-42-ans-apres |archive-date=2012-05-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Prior to the 2011–12 season, the club had never suffered relegation from the country's top division. Dijon returned to the second division after only one season in [[Ligue 1]], while Caen fell to the second tier after two years in the first division.

== Teams ==

There were three promoted teams from [[Ligue 2]], replacing the three teams that were relegated from Ligue 1 following the [[2010–11 Ligue 1|2010–11 season]]. A total of 20 teams competed in the league with three clubs suffering relegation to the second division, Ligue 2. All clubs that secured Ligue 1 status for the season were subject to approval by the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]] before becoming eligible to participate.<ref name = dncg_rulings>The DNCG is responsible for overseeing the legal and financial accounts of professional football clubs in France. If clubs operating in [[French football]] don't meet the DNCG's expectations, they can face sanctions, such as relegation.</ref>

[[AC Arles-Avignon|Arles-Avignon]] was the first club to suffer relegation from the first division to Ligue 2. The club's impending drop occurred on 17 April 2011 following the team's 2–0 defeat to [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco]]. The negative result made it mathematically impossible for Arles to seize the 17th position in the table, which would have allowed the club to remain in Ligue 1. Arles-Avignon made its return to Ligue 2 after only a year's spell in the top division of French football.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arles-Avignon relégué en Ligue 2 |url=http://fr.sports.yahoo.com/17042011/1/arles-avignon-relegue-en-ligue-2.html |publisher=[[Yahoo!]] |date=17 April 2011 |access-date=23 April 2011 |language=fr }}{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On 15 May, [[RC Lens|Lens]] were relegated from the first division to Ligue 2 after its 1–1 draw with Monaco. Lens returned to Ligue 2 for the first time since the [[2008–09 Ligue 2|2008–09 season]] when the club finished as champions of the league.<ref>{{cite news |title=Marseille lâche prise, Lens relégué en L2 |url=http://www.20minutes.fr/article/724295/ligue-1-marseille-lache-prise-lens-relegue-l2 |publisher=20 Minutes |date=15 May 2011 |access-date=17 May 2011 | language = fr}}</ref> On the final day of the Ligue 1 season, Monaco suffered relegation to the second division after losing 2–0 to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]]. The club's appearance in Ligue 2 was its first since 1976.<ref>{{cite news |title=Monaco relégué en L2 |url=http://www.eurosport.fr/football/ligue-1/2010-2011/monaco-relegue-en-l2_sto2814211/flashnews.shtml |publisher=[[Eurosport]] |date=29 May 2011 |access-date=29 May 2011 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110601011648/http://www.eurosport.fr/football/ligue-1/2010-2011/monaco-relegue-en-l2_sto2814211/flashnews.shtml |archive-date=2011-06-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[Evian Thonon Gaillard FC|Evian]] became the first club from Ligue 2 to achieve promotion to Ligue 1 after its 2–1 victory over [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] on 20 May 2011.<ref>{{cite news |title=L'Evian TG FC en Ligue 1! |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue2/article/l-evian-tg-fc-en-ligue-1.htm |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=20 May 2011 |access-date=20 May 2011 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120526094616/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue2/article/l-evian-tg-fc-en-ligue-1.htm |archive-date=2012-05-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Evian made its debut in the first division and, similar to Arles-Avignon the previous season, the club's ascension to the first division is notable due in part to the fact that it has achieved successive promotions in four straight seasons. On the final day of the Ligue 2 season, both [[Dijon FCO|Dijon]] and [[AC Ajaccio|Ajaccio]] earned berths in the first division after posting positive results in their respective matches.<ref>{{cite news |title=L'Evian TG FC champion, l'AC Ajaccio et le Dijon FCO en Ligue 1 |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue2/article/l-evian-tg-fc-champion-l-ac-ajaccio-et-le-dijon-fco-en-ligue-1.htm |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=27 May 2011 |access-date=27 May 2011 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120530002102/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue2/article/l-evian-tg-fc-champion-l-ac-ajaccio-et-le-dijon-fco-en-ligue-1.htm |archive-date=2012-05-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Dijon was promoted despite losing on the match day and, similar to Évian, made its debut in the top division of French football. Ajaccio returned to Ligue 1 after five seasons in the second division.

*First goal of the season: [[Anthony Mounier]] for Nice against Lyon (<small>''6 August 2011''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |title=Ligue 1: 1ere journée: Lyon est leader, Paris déçoit |url=http://www.chronofoot.com/ligue-1/ligue-1-1ere-journee-lyon-est-leader-paris-decoit_art16917.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317030541/http://www.chronofoot.com/ligue-1/ligue-1-1ere-journee-lyon-est-leader-paris-decoit_art16917.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 March 2012 |work=Chronofoot |language=fr |date=6 August 2011 |access-date=9 August 2011 }}</ref>

Lyon Match Report |url=http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/74412 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |date=10 September 2011 |access-date=15 September 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910021325/http://new.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/74412 |archive-date=10 September 2012 }}</ref>

=== Discipline ===

=== Annual awards ===

==== UNFP Ligue 1 Player of the Year ====

The  UNFP Ligue 1 Player of the Year was awarded to [[Eden Hazard]].<ref name="unfp_awards">{{cite news|title=UNFP: Trophées UNFP du football: Le palmarès complet... |url=http://www.unfp.org/a-la-une/article/le-palmares-complet-14052012-6476.html |publisher=[[National Union of Professional Footballers]] |date=14 May 2012 |access-date=14 May 2012 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140303055426/http://www.unfp.org/a-la-une/article/le-palmares-complet-14052012-6476.html |archive-date=3 March 2014 }}</ref>

==== UNFP Young Player of the Year ====

The  UNFP Young Player of the Year was awarded to [[Younès Belhanda]].<ref name="unfp_awards"/>

==== UNFP Ligue 1 Goalkeeper of the Year ====

The UNFP Goalkeeper of the Year was awarded to [[Hugo Lloris]].<ref name="unfp_awards"/>
